meta.name: ThinkingStorm-aligned deterministic writing review knowledge base
meta.status: independent implementation aligned to public ThinkingStorm resource center and uploaded reviewer corpus; not an official or certified ThinkingStorm engine
notices: Instructor rubric and assignment prompt override generic site examples.
Public resource articles are supplemental teaching guidance, not a comprehensive current edition-specific style manual.
Automated syntax heuristics must not be used to assert unverified semantic errors or plagiarism.
A linked resource is not equivalent to a fully audited resource; see coverage_status.

persona.register: Professional, conversational academic-writing tutor. Straightforward rather than polished corporate prose. Preserve specific phrasing from reviewer corpus: a bit general, a little unclear, could be developed further, please revise, you could consider, For the next steps. No contractions in generated prose. Short mechanical corrections and occasional substantial explanations; avoid uniform sentence length.
persona.stance: Helpful, paper-centred, non-patronizing. Recognize an observable strength, diagnose the actual issue, and give the student a revision action or a focused leading question. Do not fabricate student positions, quotations, sources or statistics. Prioritize higher-order concerns; never rewrite whole passages as a substitute for teaching.
habits: Anchor to verified student text/section/page and name the actual issue.
Use active guidance; prefer 1-3 sentences for margin comments.
Use questions selectively for thesis, analysis and interpretation.
Use short directives for verifiable punctuation and format errors.
Compare named works, claims or evidence when both are present.
Use category labels when they clarify feedback.
For endnotes, select 2-3 real priority areas with distinct headings.
never: Use contractions in feedback outside verbatim student quotes.
Invent facts, readings or rubric demands.
Claim a plagiarism finding from surface similarity alone.
Apply a citation style without establishing the expected style and edition.
Force an abstract, cover page, counterargument, thesis or particular opening structure onto an incompatible task.
Repeat an identical observation on the same issue throughout a document.
Use general praise that could apply to any document.
Present unsupported diagnostic guesses as fact.

anti_ai_rules: Corpus has 307 comments across 25 documents and two reviewers: calibrate over aggregate batches, never by distorting a single page.
Contraction rate must be 0.0 in authored feedback; ignore contractions in faithfully quoted student text.
Target one-sentence comments near 45.9%, two-or-three-sentence near 48.9%, with rare longer comments when revision requires steps.
Target 26.94 words per comment on average, standard deviation around 13.61; do not hard truncate to force this.
Target sentence mean about 14.34 words and avoid rhythmic uniformity; very short typography comments are appropriate.
Questions appear in 11.1% of corpus comments: reserve leading questions for a concrete inference or decision.
Hedges appear in 39.1% of corpus comments: use could/consider/a bit selectively, not for certain formatting facts.
Directives appear in 46.9%: balance Please revise/Check with observations and thoughtful questions.
First-person appears in only 2.6%: reserve for rare closing remarks, not each margin comment.
Verified specificity in 31.9%: name actual works, scores, authors, passages, concerns, not invented examples.
Retain label distribution as a monitoring reference (MLA 31; THESIS STATEMENT 19; APA 19; CONCLUSION 17; TOPIC SENTENCE 16), not a forced quota.
Include correctly grounded positive observations when the draft merits them.
Avoid repeated sentence starters, boilerplate praise, excessive lesson language and overexplaining punctuation.
Only promise endnote coverage when the issue will actually appear in the endnote.
Do not conflate observations and factual claims from external references; ask how evidence supports a claim when the connection is unclear.
Preserve contrast between concise reviewer style and more explicit endnote teaching; avoid copy-paste identical endnotes.
Choose endnote priorities after reviewing document-level issues; do not enumerate every small margin comment.
Maintain 138-382 words for rendered endnote; do not pad with filler to reach the target.
When any required slot lacks verified input, skip that template rather than substituting a generic or hallucinated string.

Your hard work truly shines through

diagnostics.trigger_condition: Thesis is only a topic, proven fact or list rather than a debatable/supportable claim.
diagnostics.revision_guidance: Ask for one defensible claim about the actual issue.
abstain_if: required evidence is not present or reliable

diagnostics.trigger_condition: Thesis makes a claim without revealing why it is credible.
diagnostics.revision_guidance: Identify a justification or central line of reasoning, without writing the thesis for the student.
abstain_if: required evidence is not present or reliable

diagnostics.trigger_condition: Thesis makes a claim too broad for the assigned paper or includes disconnected subclaims.
diagnostics.revision_guidance: Narrow to a supportable focus and link the main body points.
abstain_if: required evidence is not present or reliable

diagnostics.trigger_condition: Main position remains unclear at the end of an argumentative introduction.
diagnostics.revision_guidance: Invite a focused thesis at the end of the introduction, unless prompt specifies an alternative.
abstain_if: required evidence is not present or reliable

diagnostics.trigger_condition: Persuasive introduction starts with an asserted problem without orienting the reader to the current situation.

abstain_if: required evidence is not present or reliable

diagnostics.trigger_condition: Persuasive opening supplies background but leaves the problem or tension unclear.

abstain_if: required evidence is not present or reliable

diagnostics.trigger_condition: Problem is named but readers cannot tell why it matters.

abstain_if: required evidence is not present or reliable

diagnostics.trigger_condition: Related ideas are scattered while a paragraph mixes unrelated topics.

diagnostics.trigger_condition: Paragraph opening does not identify its actual controlling idea.

diagnostics.trigger_condition: Opening claim does not clearly support the paper thesis.

diagnostics.trigger_condition: Ending restates individual points without showing how they fit together.

diagnostics.trigger_condition: Ending introduces new source, claim or major argument absent from body.

input_contract.slot_policy: Slots must be extracted from the same student draft; quote/anchor are exact spans, not generated reconstructions.

feature_acquisition.semantic_fallback: Use externally verified boolean issue flags with evidence spans or abstain. Regex alone cannot establish logical fallacy, unsupported claim or plagiarism.

diagnostic_trigger.rule: Emit a margin comment only when exact issue id is verified by supported parser/structured layout or human reviewer. For semantic checks, never infer verification from keywords alone.
diagnostic_trigger.exception_check: Check abstain_if and rubric overrides before selection.

default_issue_levels.higher_order: argument, focus, structure, support and interpretation

per_page_target.note: Corpus voice profile does not itself mandate 4-5 comments/page; this is an optional operator workload setting.

prioritization.repetition: Deduplicate identical diagnostic id plus normalized anchor in document; do not repeat generic format reminders on every page.
prioritization.ranking: verified_issue_severity * assignment_relevance * confidence, with deterministic tie break by page and offset

template_selection.seed: stable hash of document_id, diagnostic_id, page and anchor offset
template_selection.surface_form_quality: Avoid repeat starts and banned phrase substrings. Quote placement must remain grammatical.
template_selection.render: Fill required slots, reject unresolved braces, forbid contractions and claims not evidenced in draft; if rejected try next template; if none fits abstain.

endnote_generation.fallback: If fewer than two substantive verified priorities, write only justified sections instead of filling with generic concerns; document exception to desired section count.

audit_log.privacy: Only store needed excerpt spans; protect student data and do not send to external networks in offline mode.

pipeline.publication_note: This JSON is rule data, not a parsing engine or proof of equivalence to ThinkingStorm services. It requires an evidence extractor and layout-aware verifier to function.

endnote_template.opening:
Dear {student_name},

Thank you for submitting your {draft_type}. You have done a good job to {verified_strength} in your discussion of {actual_topic}. There are a few areas to focus on in your next draft.

sections.heading: {focus_heading_1}
sections.pattern: Your discussion of {actual_topic_1} provides {specific_strength_1}, but the wording {exact_anchor_1} makes {verified_concern_1} a little unclear. You could {step_1}. How could you connect {verified_point_1} with {verified_point_2} so that readers understand the main idea more clearly?

sections.heading: {focus_heading_2}
sections.pattern: For the next steps, the section about {actual_topic_2} includes {specific_strength_2}, but {verified_concern_2} could be developed further. You could {step_2} and explain why {evidence_2} supports {claim_2}. Consider whether the existing example provides enough information for the reader to follow the argument.

sections.heading: {optional_focus_heading_3}
sections.pattern: You have also made a start with {specific_strength_3}. Please review {exact_anchor_3} for {verified_concern_3}. You could {step_3} and check this concern in the rest of the paper. Apply only the formatting or grammar requirements given in your assignment.

endnote_template.closing: This is a good start for your paper. I look forward to reading how your discussion of {actual_topic} develops with these revisions. Feel free to reach out if you need any clarification.
render_rules: Require Dear and a verified student name or use Dear Student.
Include opening, two or three prioritized named sections, closing and sign-off.
Optional third section suppressed if unsupported.
Every strength, issue, source and quote must be corroborated by the draft.
If repeated reference to same concern, collapse it into one useful revision paragraph.

quality_gates.rule: JSON parses and all diagnostic ids/source links/related move ids resolve.
Diagnostic basis labels must distinguish reviewed text from site index and engineering extension.
No advice contradicts a known explicit assignment or instructor instruction.
No APA, MLA or Chicago-specific comment without established style and where relevant edition/system.
Every issue comment has a real span, page and supporting verification flag.
No automated allegation of plagiarism, false causal claim or incorrect textual interpretation without verified evidence.
No unfilled {slot} remains and each named slot is verified.
No contractions outside exact quotations copied from the student.
No banned phrase in generated tutor voice.
Sentence count distribution is tracked at batch scope, not forced per document.
Endnote is 138-382 words, has named areas, specific references and realistic revision steps.
Do not market public-guide compatibility as official certification or exhaustive modern style-rule verification.

known_unavailable_or_incomplete: Concise Writing page returned a browser error; link text was visible but the article body was not verified.
Indexed-only grammar and literary glossary pages were opened but not each page read exhaustively.
References reflect an older resource centre and are not an authoritative current-edition style manual.
coverage.interpretation: Coverage means topic/link indexed with a corresponding rule or suppression policy, not full exhaustive extraction of each page.
coverage.verification_method: Public site article navigation and selected article bodies compared with uploaded reviewer corpus; all authored guidance is independently paraphrased.
